formation.title: The Founding of the Luba Empire
formation.text:
The marshy grasslands of the Upemba Depression have given rise to something extraordinary. From the lakeshores where our ancestors fished and smelted iron, from the copper-rich hills where our smiths forge the distinctive cross-shaped ingots that serve as currency across central Africa, a great kingdom has emerged. The descendants of Kalala Ilunga, the mythical hunter who overthrew the tyrant Kongolo Mwamba, now rule from Mwibele over a realm of diverse peoples bound by shared institutions.

But two visions compete for the soul of this new empire. The Mulopwe sits enthroned as a living deity, his authority absolute and sacred, yet beside him stands the Bambudye council, guardians of the lukasa memory boards, with the power to check, counsel, and even depose a king who abuses his mandate. Will the Luba Empire be forged through the divine fire of royal authority, or built upon the enduring wisdom of its institutions?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: The Mulopwe's word is law; our divine king shall rule unchallenged.

modifiers.name: Divine Authority of the Mulopwe
modifiers.text: The sacred king rules as a living deity whose word is law. Through divine mandate and iron will, the Mulopwe commands absolute loyalty from his Balopwe clan kings, extracting tribute and enforcing obedience across the savanna.

options.text: The Bambudye shall guide us. No king rules without the council's wisdom.

modifiers.name: Wisdom of the Bambudye
modifiers.text: The Bambudye council guides the state with accumulated knowledge encoded in the lukasa memory boards. No ruler may act without their counsel, and no chief may hold office without first mastering the society's teachings. This institutional resilience has allowed the Luba to absorb foreign peoples and survive succession crises that would shatter lesser kingdoms.

advances.name: Upemba Ironworking
advances.text: The iron-working traditions of the Upemba Depression, refined over centuries of continuous habitation, produce weapons and tools of exceptional quality.

advances.name: Kilolo Administration
advances.text: Village chiefs known as Kilolo manage local affairs, collect tribute, and maintain granaries that sustain the population through lean seasons.

advances.name: Lake Fishing Tradition
advances.text: The organized fishing communities of the Upemba lakes, continuing the ancient Kisalian tradition, form the economic backbone of early Luba settlement.

advances.name: Palm Oil Trade
advances.text:
Every village keeps its grove of palms. They are pressed for oil, used for cooking, lighting, and trade across central Africa, tapped for wine, and stripped for raffia.

Available in: Palm Grove

advances.name: Ancestral Spirit Tradition
advances.text: The veneration of ancestral spirits provides a common religious framework that binds diverse Luba communities together across the savanna.

advances.name: Lineage Chiefs
advances.text: The system of governance through lineage heads creates a durable hierarchy that can incorporate new peoples while maintaining order.

advances.name: Balopwe Royal Institution
advances.text: The sacred institution of the Balopwe, clan kings who serve as intermediaries between the divine Mulopwe and the people, forms the backbone of Luba military and political power.

advances.name: Bambudye Knowledge Tradition
advances.text: The Bambudye secret society, guardians of the lukasa memory boards, preserves and transmits the accumulated knowledge of the Luba state.

event.title: The Keepers of the Lukasa
event.text:
The Bambudye society has reached a new level of sophistication. Their memory boards, the lukasa, are masterworks of encoded knowledge. Court historians known as bana balute run their fingertips across surfaces studded with beads and shells, each cluster representing a king, a migration, a law, or a sacred site. Three types of lukasa now exist: the lukasa lwa nkunda recording mythical heroes and migration routes, the lukasa lwa kabemba organizing the Mbudye society itself, and secret boards created for individual rulers containing knowledge too dangerous for common ears.

No candidate for political office may receive their title without first becoming a member of the Bambudye. The society serves as living constitution, historical archive, and check on royal power, all encoded in boards small enough to hold in one hand.

options.text: The memory of the Luba shall endure through all ages.

advances.name: Copper Cross Currency
advances.text:
The distinctive cross-shaped copper ingots cast by Luba smiths serve as currency across central African trade networks.

Available in: Royal Copper Smithy

event.title: The Copper Cross Standard
event.text: Our smiths have perfected the art of casting the distinctive cross-shaped copper ingots known as handa. Weighing from a few grams to over a kilogram, these crosses have become the standard currency not just of our markets but of trade networks stretching from the equatorial forests to the Zambezi. Songye merchants barter raffia cloth for our copper; traders from the east bring shells and beads. The question before us is how to leverage this monetary supremacy: shall we expand our copper production to dominate regional commerce, or use our economic power to bind more peoples into our tributary network?

options.text: Expand the copper trade. Let the handa flow to every market.

modifiers.name: Copper Cross Economy
modifiers.text: The distinctive cross-shaped copper ingots of the Luba have become the currency of central African trade, accepted from the forests of the Congo to the shores of the Indian Ocean.

options.text: Bind more tributaries; copper buys loyalty, not just goods.

modifiers.name: Tributary Hegemony
modifiers.text: Rather than minting currency, the Luba state has channeled its copper wealth into building a vast tributary network. Subject peoples render manpower and resources in exchange for the protection and prestige of the Mulopwe's authority.

advances.name: Divine Kingship Shrines
advances.text: Deceased Mulopwe become deities, and their former capitals transform into living shrines that sanctify the landscape and legitimate royal authority.

advances.name: Kalala Ilunga's Legacy
advances.text: All rulers of the Luba trace their ancestry to Kalala Ilunga, the mythical hunter who overthrew Kongolo Mwamba and introduced advanced iron forging and royal political practices.

advances.name: Tributary Expansion
advances.text: Luba armies target population-dense regions to extract tribute, expanding the empire's reach and military reserves.

advances.name: Twite Military Reform
advances.text: The twite, the Mulopwe's military chief, reorganizes the provincial armies into a more professional force capable of sustained campaigns.

advances.name: Copper and Salt Routes
advances.text: Control of the vital trade routes linking copper mines, salt sources, and agricultural regions consolidates Luba economic power.

advances.name: Katanga Salt Control
advances.text:
The salt marshes of the southern territories become a critical state monopoly, driving both economic growth and political competition.

Available in: Salt Works

advances.name: Raffia Textile Industry
advances.text:
The weaving of raffia palm fibers into cloth creates a major export commodity, traded to the Songye and other neighboring peoples.

Available in: Palm Grove

advances.name: Savanna Fortification
advances.text: Fortified village palisades protect Luba settlements from raiders, using the natural advantages of the savanna landscape.

advances.name: Lualaba River Network
advances.text: The Lualaba River and its tributaries serve as the empire's highways, carrying trade goods, tribute, and information between the heartland and distant provinces.

advances.name: Tribute Army Reform
advances.text: The tribute collection system is militarized, with dedicated forces that can rapidly deploy to enforce obligations across the empire's extensive domains.

advances.name: Lunda Model Spread
advances.text: The Luba model of sacred kingship and institutional governance spreads to neighboring peoples, most notably the Lunda, creating a vast zone of Luba-influenced statecraft.

event.title: The Spread of the Balopwe Model
event.text:
The Luba system of sacred kingship has proven so effective that neighboring peoples have adopted it wholesale. The Lunda kingdom, our most powerful offshoot, has carried the balopwe model of governance across a vast swathe of central Africa, from northern Angola to northwestern Zambia. Foreign leaders and governments are incorporated through the flexible system of clan kingship, where loyalty to the Mulopwe and membership in the Bambudye creates bonds stronger than ethnicity or language.

This is the true genius of Luba statecraft: a government durable enough to withstand succession disputes, yet flexible enough to absorb entire foreign polities. The balopwe model is not merely a form of rule: it is an idea, spreading like fire across the savanna.

options.text: Our model of governance shall be the standard of central Africa.

advances.name: Copper Belt Consolidation
advances.text:
The rich copper deposits connecting Luba territory to the Zambian copperbelt are brought under tighter state control, fueling imperial expansion.

Available in: Copper Diggings

advances.name: Bamfumu Nobility
advances.text: The Bamfumu court nobles gain formalized powers and responsibilities, creating a stable aristocratic class that supports the Mulopwe's rule.

advances.name: Sacred Geography
advances.text: The landscape itself becomes a map of Luba spirituality, with shrines, sacred groves, and ancestral sites marking the geography of divine kingship.

advances.name: Advanced Smelting Techniques
advances.text:
Luba metalworkers develop techniques for producing sheet iron and soldering metals, enabling the creation of the double iron bells that symbolize royal power.

Available in: Royal Copper Smithy

advances.name: Mulopwe Centralization
advances.text: The Mulopwe consolidates direct authority over formerly autonomous provinces, reducing the independence of local Kilolo chiefs.

advances.name: Katanga Copper Hegemony
advances.text: Complete control of the Katanga copper sources makes the Luba Empire the undisputed master of central African metallurgy and trade.

advances.name: Savanna Road Networks
advances.text: Organized paths connecting major settlements improve the movement of goods, tribute, and armies across the vast savanna territories.

advances.name: Mbudye Judicial Reform
advances.text: The Bambudye society formalizes its role as the supreme judicial authority, with the power to interpret law and even depose kings who abuse their mandate.

advances.name: Cross-Continental Trade
advances.text: Luba trade networks extend from the equatorial forests to the Indian Ocean coast, connecting central Africa to global commerce.

advances.name: Warrior Societies
advances.text: Organized warrior societies provide the Luba with a disciplined military elite trained in the tactics of savanna warfare. The client kings who hold the Mulopwe's sacred fire send their warbands to his wars.

advances.name: Anti-Colonial Resistance
advances.text: The warriors of the Luba heartland leverage their knowledge of local terrain and guerrilla tactics to resist foreign encroachment. Ivory sold to the coast traders buys the muskets they do it with.

event.title: Defenders of the Heartland
event.text: Foreign powers have cast their eyes upon the riches of our copper belt and the labor of our people. But the warriors of the Luba heartland know every path through the Upemba wetlands, every ford across the Lualaba, every defensive position in the savanna hills. What outsiders see as impenetrable bush, our soldiers call home. The Mulopwe has called upon the warrior societies to organize a defense that turns the landscape itself into a weapon, hostile terrain, stretched supply lines, and the implacable resistance of a people fighting for their sacred homeland.

advances.name: Copper Industrial Revolution
advances.text: The application of new techniques to Luba copper extraction and smelting transforms the ancient industry into a modern economic engine.

advances.name: Unified Luba Governance
advances.text: The Mulopwe's authority and the Bambudye's wisdom merge into a unified system of governance capable of administering a modern state.

advances.name: Modern Trade Networks
advances.text: Traditional Luba trade routes are expanded and modernized, integrating the empire into global commercial systems.

advances.name: Luba Cultural Renaissance
advances.text: A flowering of Luba art, sculpture, and oral literature celebrates the empire's heritage and projects its cultural influence across central Africa. Court carvers cut the caryatid stools, bow stands and headrests that seat and arm a king.

advances.name: Sovereignty of the Heartland
advances.text: The Luba Empire asserts its sovereignty as an independent power, demanding recognition from the great powers of the world.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Luba Empire
destiny.text: The Luba Empire stands at a crossroads. The path chosen at its founding now beckons the nation toward its ultimate destiny. Stability and purpose are required before the great work can begin.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Destiny Beckons
event.text: Our empire has achieved the stability needed to pursue its greater purpose. The path we chose at our founding, whether the divine authority of the Mulopwe or the institutional wisdom of the Bambudye, now calls us forward. The ancestors watch, and the lukasa boards record our deeds for posterity. Let the great work begin.

options.text: The destiny of the Luba unfolds before us.

destiny.name: The March to Tanganyika
destiny.text: The Mulopwe demands expansion eastward to the shores of Lake Tanganyika and northward into the Lomami basin. These conquests, made with warriors armed in Luba iron from weapon guilds in two of our towns, will establish the military foundations of a continental empire.

conditions.text: Chose Divine Authority of the Mulopwe
Own Ujiji, or a subject owns it
Own Lussuna, or a subject owns it
At least 2 owned locations have a Weapon Guild or a building that replaced it

event.title: The Eastern Frontier
event.text: Our armies have reached the shores of Lake Tanganyika, and the Lomami basin bows to the Mulopwe's authority. The peoples of the east, long accustomed to their independence, now acknowledge the divine king whose iron weapons and copper crosses have followed the trade routes into their lands. The warriors return laden with tribute, ivory, copper, and the loyalty of new subjects.

options.text: The Mulopwe's writ runs to the great lake.

destiny.name: The Fall of Kongo
destiny.text: With the east secured, the Mulopwe turns his gaze westward. The great kingdom of Kongo must be brought under Luba suzerainty: its capital at Mbanza Kongo and half of its heartland are to be held, with the royal guard of the Balopwe at the head of the army.

conditions.text: Own Mbanza Kongo, or a subject owns it
Renaissance or later
We or our non-sovereign subjects hold at least 50% of the locations in Kongo

event.title: The Kongo Has Fallen
event.text: Mbanza Kongo, the ancient seat of power in the west, has been taken. The Mulopwe's banner flies over a city that once rivaled our own in prestige and influence. This is no mere conquest: it is the subjugation of a civilization. How shall we consolidate this immense prize? We may strip its wealth to fuel further campaigns, or we may honor its warriors by integrating them into the Luba military tradition.

options.text: Strip the conquered lands of their tribute.

modifiers.name: Conqueror's Tribute
modifiers.text: The spoils of the Kongo conquest fuel further expansion, though the costs of administering such vast territories strain the treasury.

options.text: Honor the fallen, integrate their warriors.

modifiers.name: Warrior's Prestige
modifiers.text: The integration of Kongo warriors into Luba military tradition has produced a battle-hardened force with superior morale and tactical flexibility.

destiny.name: Mulopwe Supreme
destiny.text: The final ambition of the divine king: to push beyond the interior and seize the coastal trade cities of Kilwa and Sofala, connecting the Luba heartland to the wealth of the Indian Ocean. This is the apex of sacred conquest.

conditions.text: Own Kilwa, or a subject owns it
Own Sofala, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75
Gold at least 3000

event.title: The Mulopwe Ascendant
event.text:
The sacred king has achieved what the ancestors could only dream. From the Upemba Depression to the Indian Ocean, from the Lomami to the Zambezi, the Luba Empire now controls the trade routes that connect the African interior to the wider world. Kilwa's dhows carry Luba copper to Arabia, and Sofala's gold flows through the Mulopwe's hands. This is the apex of divine kingship, an empire built on iron, copper, and the sacred mandate of the ancestors.

Shall the Mulopwe rule from an iron throne of military supremacy, or shall he forge an empire of copper, wealthy, stable, and enduring?

options.text: The Iron Throne shall command all nations.

modifiers.name: The Iron Throne
modifiers.text: The Mulopwe rules from an iron throne, his divine authority unchallenged across a vast empire. Military supremacy is total, though the costs of perpetual war drive inflation upward.

options.text: The Empire of Copper endures through wealth.

modifiers.name: Empire of Copper
modifiers.text: The wealth of the copper belt and the coastal trade cities sustains a vast army, and the subject kings of the Mulopwe pay their tribute in copper.

destiny.name: The Knowledge Keepers
destiny.text: The Bambudye council directs the nation toward institutional development and economic mastery. Raise Baluba, the royal seat, into a town where the court keeps its memory, and ensure that Luba copper dominates the markets.

conditions.text: Chose Wisdom of the Bambudye
We own Baluba and it is a town or larger
Gold at least 1000
The capital

children.text: Copper is produced in the market
Copper is traded in the market

event.title: The Knowledge Economy
event.text: The Bambudye council has guided the nation toward a new model of power, one built not on conquest alone, but on institutional knowledge and economic sophistication. Baluba has grown into a royal town, and from its court the copper cross has become a tool of power as well as a trade good. The lukasa boards now record not just genealogies and migration stories, but trade agreements, market prices, and diplomatic protocols. Knowledge is the truest form of wealth.

options.text: The wisdom of the Bambudye enriches us all.

destiny.name: Lords of the Trade Routes
destiny.text: Extend the Bambudye's commercial vision to the Atlantic coast. The port of Loango will serve as the western terminus of a Luba trade network stretching from copper mines to ocean harbors, with Luba merchants at work in three markets.

conditions.text: Own Loango, or a subject owns it
We have merchants in at least 3 markets, or at least 3 owned locations have a Luba Trade Post
Prestige at least 50

event.title: The Atlantic Connection
event.text:
Our merchants have reached Loango on the Atlantic coast, completing a trade route that stretches from the copper mines of Katanga to the harbors of the western ocean. Luba copper crosses, raffia cloth, and ivory now flow westward through a network of intermediaries, while foreign goods (salt, shells, and cloth from distant lands) flow back to enrich the heartland.

Shall we focus on building merchant houses along the copper routes, or shall we use salt and diplomacy to bind our trading partners into a durable alliance network?

options.text: Build the merchant houses; copper is king.

modifiers.name: Copper Merchants
modifiers.text: Luba merchant houses dominate the copper trade from Katanga to the Atlantic, converting local peoples to Luba commercial practices. Success, however, breeds a certain complacency.

options.text: Salt and diplomacy forge stronger bonds.

modifiers.name: Salt Diplomacy
modifiers.text: The exchange of salt and copper has forged a web of diplomatic relationships that extends Luba influence without the costs of conquest, though maintaining these relationships demands expensive courtly displays.

destiny.name: Bambudye Supreme
destiny.text: The ultimate expression of the Bambudye's institutional wisdom: a trade empire spanning the continent, where ivory flows through Luba markets and houses of memory in three locations, libraries or Lukasa Archives, keep the memory of the realm. This is governance triumphant.

conditions.text: At least 3 owned locations have a Library, or at least 3 have a Lukasa Archive
Gold at least 3000
Prestige at least 75
A market the country is in

children.text: Ivory is produced in the market
Ivory is traded in the market

event.title: The Bambudye Triumphant
event.text:
The Bambudye society has achieved something unprecedented: a governance system so effective, so flexible, and so deeply rooted in institutional knowledge that it has become a model for peoples across the continent. Foreign leaders seek membership in the council, and the lukasa boards are studied as masterworks of encoded wisdom. The Luba Empire has proven that a state built on knowledge and trade can rival any built on conquest.

Shall we formalize the Bambudye as a constitutional body, or shall we project Luba culture outward, absorbing neighboring peoples into our institutional framework?

options.text: The Bambudye is our living constitution.

modifiers.name: Living Constitution
modifiers.text: The Bambudye council functions as a living constitution, providing institutional continuity, diplomatic expertise, and the capacity to recover from any crisis.

options.text: Let all peoples learn the Luba way.

modifiers.name: Cultural Hegemony
modifiers.text: The Luba model of governance spreads to every corner of central Africa, absorbing foreign peoples into a shared institutional framework that reduces tensions and enables flexible policy-making.

units.name: Ironworker Warriors
units.text: Village militia armed with weapons forged from Upemba iron, spears, axes, and short swords of exceptional quality. These farmer-soldiers carry the iron-working tradition of their ancestors into battle.

units.name: Balopwe Royal Guard
units.text: The personal retinue of the sacred king, drawn from the most loyal Balopwe clan warriors. Their devotion to the Mulopwe transcends ordinary military loyalty; they fight as if defending a living god.

units.name: Twite's Spearmen
units.text: Provincial soldiers organized under the twite, the Mulopwe's military chief. Equipped with long spears and wooden shields, they form the disciplined backbone of Luba field armies.

units.name: Tribute Collectors
units.text: Fast-moving armed detachments tasked with enforcing tributary obligations across the empire. Lightly equipped for rapid marches, they can project Luba authority deep into subject territories.

units.name: Warbands of the Fire Kings
units.text: The men a client king owes the Mulopwe. A chief who has taken the sacred fire from the royal hearth rules by that grant, and answers the call to war with his own spearmen.

units.name: Musketeers of the Ivory Trade
units.text: Warriors armed with trade muskets bought for ivory from the caravans of the east coast. The guns are worn and the powder is never enough, but these men know every path of the savanna and fight from cover on their own ground.

buildings.name: Lukasa Archive
buildings.text: A center of Bambudye learning where master historians guard and interpret the lukasa memory boards, preserving the genealogies, laws, and migration stories of the Luba people.

buildings.name: Royal Copper Smithy
buildings.text: An advanced metalworking workshop where Luba smiths cast the distinctive cross-shaped copper ingots that serve as currency across central African trade networks.

buildings.name: Mulopwe's Shrine
buildings.text: A living shrine built at the former capital of a deceased Mulopwe, who upon death became a deity. These sacred sites sanctify the landscape and reinforce the divine legitimacy of royal authority.

buildings.name: Kilolo's Granary
buildings.text: An administrative storehouse managed by the local Kilolo chief, collecting and redistributing agricultural tribute to sustain the population and fund the state.

buildings.name: Luba Trade Post
buildings.text: A regional trading station positioned on the copper and salt routes, facilitating exchange between the Luba heartland and distant trading partners.

buildings.name: Upemba Fishery
buildings.text: An organized lakeside fishing operation on the Upemba Depression lakes, providing a reliable food surplus that sustains the surrounding population.

where.text: The location's raw material is Fish

buildings.name: Luba Palisade
buildings.text: A fortified village defense constructed from hardwood logs, designed to protect settlements from raiders and serve as a rally point for local militia.

buildings.name: Carvers' Atelier
buildings.text: A court workshop where master carvers and their pupils work in one recognisable hand. The atelier of the Master of Buli, with its long, worn faces, is the best known of them.

buildings.name: Palm Grove
buildings.text: The stand of raffia and oil palms kept by a village. The palms are tapped for wine, pressed for oil, and stripped for the fiber that is woven into cloth.

buildings.name: Salt Works
buildings.text: A boiling place at the edge of a salt marsh. The salt cakes made here are carried north along the Lualaba and traded for iron, fish, and cloth.

children.text: Salt is produced in the market

buildings.name: Copper Diggings
buildings.text: Open pits where the green ore of Katanga is dug. The smelters cast the metal into crosses before it leaves the site.

where.text: The location's raw material is Copper

buildings.name: Mulopwe's War Camp
buildings.text: A permanent military encampment established by the divine king's twite, from which armies are mustered, supplied, and dispatched to enforce the Mulopwe's will across distant frontiers.

buildings.name: Grand Lukasa Council
buildings.text: The supreme hall of the Bambudye society, where the most sacred lukasa boards are studied and the wisest councillors guide the governance of a continental trade empire.

list.name: Bilumbu Spirit-Medium Council
list.text: The bilumbu were spirit mediums who divined ancestral judgement using the kashekesheke divinatory rod, ruling on succession disputes, witchcraft accusations, and tributary obligations the Mulopwe could not address directly. Documented across the Upemba savanna from at least the sixteenth century, the bilumbu functioned as an ecclesiastical-judicial branch parallel to the secular kilolo administrators, granting verdicts that no chief dared dispute because they came from the throne's deceased predecessors. When the institution decayed, divination became a tool of factional bilumbu lineages rather than the sacred king.

list.name: Mwadi Royal Vessels
list.text: The Mwadi were senior women who, by spirit-possession ritual, incarnated deceased royal ancestresses and outranked living chiefs by virtue of channelling the founders Kalala Ilunga and Mbidi Kiluwe. Tributary rulers across Kanyok, Kalundwe, and Hemba married Mwadi to bind themselves to the Luba royal line, integrating peripheries through ritual kinship rather than conquest. The institution centralised authority cheaply, but produced succession crises whenever rival Mwadi claimed the same incarnation, and resentful nobles accused of insufficient devotion.

list.name: Kioni Court Musicians
list.text: The kioni were not entertainers but living archives: the court musicians sang royal genealogies, transmitted edicts as drum-rhythm phrasing across the savanna, and were present at every ritual administrative act. Functioning as a chancery without writing, the kioni preserved the cultural canon of the Luba state and projected royal authority outward through performance. When royal patronage of the kioni lapsed, court memory became contested: rival genealogies proliferated, edicts grew ambiguous, and the prestige of the Mulopwe bled away with the silence of the drums.

list.name: Twite Tributary Administration
list.text: The Twite were warlord-administrators dispatched from the capital to govern tributary subkingdoms in Kanyok, Kalundwe, and the Hemba lands, collecting copper crosses, ivory, salt, and raffia for the Mulopwe. Local chiefs retained their offices but accepted Luba supervisors who oversaw tribute, mustered auxiliary forces, and enforced ritual obligations. Effective for revenue and rapid integration, the Twite system steadily produced a quasi-noble class with private retinues whose loyalty drifted whenever central oversight relaxed.

conditions.text: Owns Baluba

list.name: Kafuti Sacred Society
list.text: The Kafuti was a sacred-political sodality of initiated notables who regulated royal succession, bore the lukasa memory boards and other regalia, and bound regional aristocrats to the Mulopwe through shared ritual knowledge that uninitiated commoners could not access. Closely linked to the Bambudye and Bukibwakulu societies, the Kafuti produced a coherent ruling class across Luba and tributary lands, but its rituals walled off advancement for everyone outside the lodge, a barrier that uninitiated peasants and rival lineages experienced as theft of voice.
